name: Serina Therapeutics, Inc.

profile.description: Serina Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company built on its proprietary poly(2-oxazoline) (POZ) polymer drug-optimization platform. Lead candidate SER-252 is a POZ-apomorphine conjugate given by subcutaneous injection to provide continuous dopaminergic stimulation in advanced Parkinson's disease, currently in a Phase 1b registrational-path study. The company also licenses POZ-lipid technology for LNP delivery.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (0/3): No product has been launched in the last five years. SER-252 remains the only clinical asset, and the January 2026 IND clearance came after a clinical hold had to be resolved, recovering from a setback rather than marking a breakthrough [3][5]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI tools, AI-designed molecules, or AI-driven efficiencies are disclosed. Market Share (0/2): The company is pre-commercial, with revenue of about $130K in 2025 that appears to come from licensing rather than product sales [2]. Pipeline (1/2): The SER-252 Phase 1b design is specific (five single-ascending-dose cohorts of 8 patients, then multiple-ascending-dose cohorts), and Cohort 1 finished dosing in July 2026, but no efficacy readout or approval timeline is visible [4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Essentially all operating spend goes to R&D at a company with negligible revenue [1][2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): The purpose of using POZ chemistry to give Parkinson's patients smoother, continuous symptom control is clear and patient-centred, but resembles that of many neuroscience biotechs [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable, foundation, or community programs were found for this ~16-person company. Employee Retention (0/2): Simply Wall St puts average management tenure at about 1 year; Steve Ledger moved from interim to permanent CEO after the founder-era leadership departed [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider purchases were found; the company has funded itself through PIPEs and at-the-market equity sales [2].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: HARD RULE, liquidity floor triggered: 66,015 average daily shares x $1.67 = about $110K of daily dollar volume, far below the $1,000,000 minimum, so Infrastructure is set to 0 regardless of other metrics [7]. For reference, the mechanical metrics are also weak: ROE of -207.9% and a negative Forward P/E of -1.59 both score 0, while D/E of 20.0% would score 1.0 [7]. Revenue growth, profit margin, and PEG are not meaningful for a company with roughly $130K of annual revenue and quarterly non-GAAP losses of $0.55-0.58 per share [1][2].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): SER-252's value rests on physical polymer-conjugate chemistry, GMP manufacturing, and FDA-regulated human trials, none of which AI can substitute; regulatory approval still requires clinical evidence [3][5]. The exposure is competitive: AI-accelerated discovery at larger rivals could shorten Serina's window in continuous-delivery Parkinson's therapy, where AbbVie's Vyalev and other infusion approaches already compete. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue or AI-enabled products are disclosed [3].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Serina is a single-asset micro-cap playing a survival game, funding one clinical milestone at a time [2]. Its leadership has turned over recently, and the patient-centred purpose has not yet been tested by consistent, long-term decisions. There is too little organizational history to show trust, courage, or flexibility [6].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The cause, freeing advanced Parkinson's patients from 'off' episodes through continuous delivery, is service-oriented [3]. It is not articulated as an enduring vision beyond SER-252, and with a newly assembled leadership team there is no record of the cause surviving a leadership transition.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Persisting through the FDA clinical hold to obtain IND clearance in January 2026 shows persistence, but no costly long-term trade-off is evident; capital decisions are driven by financing needs and listing compliance [5][6].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): About 16 employees, average management tenure of about 1 year, and a string of CEO and board changes (Jay Venkatesan joined the board in February 2025; co-founder Milton Harris moved to Director Emeritus) indicate organizational flux rather than an established circle of safety [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The 2024 reverse merger with AgeX was a financing route to a public listing rather than a cause-driven reinvention. The company remains a single bet on POZ-apomorphine with no demonstrated pivot capacity if SER-252 fails [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Company communications do not discuss competitors in continuous dopaminergic therapy, such as AbbVie's subcutaneous foscarbidopa/foslevodopa or Supernus's apomorphine infusion, as a source of learning [3].

investment_thesis: Serina is a binary option on the POZ polymer platform. SER-252 aims to deliver apomorphine continuously by simple subcutaneous injection rather than pump infusion, addressing motor fluctuations in advanced Parkinson's disease, a large unmet need [3]. IND clearance in January 2026 removed the earlier clinical hold, and Cohort 1 of the Phase 1b study finished dosing in July 2026, with further single- and multiple-ascending-dose cohorts to follow [4][5]. POZ-lipid licensing for LNP delivery offers a small source of non-dilutive income, and at a roughly $42M market cap any positive PK/tolerability data or a partnership could re-rate the shares [7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is overwhelming for IOWN purposes. Daily dollar volume of about $110K fails the $1M liquidity floor by roughly 90%, making the stock untradeable at portfolio scale [7]. The company is effectively pre-revenue (about $130K in 2025), posted non-GAAP losses of $0.58 and $0.55 per share in Q1 and Q2 2026 (both worse than consensus), and has ROE of -208% [1][2][7]. Ongoing PIPE and ATM financing implies continued dilution, and the shares have fallen to $1.67 from a 50-day average of $2.20. The single-asset structure means one negative safety or PK readout could be terminal.
key_catalysts: Readouts from SER-252 Phase 1b single-ascending-dose Cohorts 2-5 on safety and PK, then the start of multiple-ascending-dose cohorts that could give first signals of reduced 'off' time [4]
A partnership or licensing deal for SER-252 or POZ-lipid LNP technology that brings non-dilutive capital and outside validation of the platform [3]
Q3 2026 results showing cash runway and any narrowing of quarterly losses after Q2's non-GAAP loss of $0.55 per share [1]
key_risks: Liquidity failure: about $110K of daily dollar volume is far below IOWN's $1M floor and widens bid-ask spreads in any sell-off [7]
Financing and dilution: with negligible revenue and persistent losses, further PIPE or ATM issuance is likely before any efficacy data, and NYSE American listing compliance remains a concern [2][6]
Single-asset clinical risk: SER-252 is the only clinical program, and it competes with approved continuous-delivery options such as AbbVie's Vyalev, raising the bar for differentiation [3]
